newsitem.title: UK: LME copper holds above $2,500 level in moribund AM.
newsitem.headline: LME copper holds above $2,500 level in moribund AM.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) base metal prices drifted in narrow ranges in dull inter-office trade on Thursday.
"It's pretty quiet across the board," a trader said, adding that market was nosing around for direction after strong gains in flagship copper and other metals earlier this week.
Three months copper was last indicated marginally firmer at $2,507/11, versus $2,506 at Wednesday's kerb close.
Cash to three months backwardation was supportive at a wider $87/$90, compared to $80/$85.
Initial resistance was expected to emerge at $2,520 and then at $2,540, while support was at $2,500 and $2,490.
However, the market was well into overbought territory, signalling that consolidation or a downwards correction may be in the offing.
"But copper could still go higher, as it seems to have found a base, and there's been a lot of spill-over into the other metals," the trader said.
In other markets, aluminium was straddling the $1,650 level after closing at $1,652 on Wednesday, and traders said it would likely follow copper's lead either higher or lower.
LME stocks showed a small decline of 1,025 tonnes, but the spread was still supportively narrow at $14/$12, compared to around $20 at the same time on Wednesday.
Lead, which powered higher on a technical rally on Wednesday, was holding tightly to its recent gains. It was last at $636, down just $1.
"Fundamentally, the three-month date is now past the worst of the seasonal demand, and current prices should attract pre-winter stockbuilding," brokers GNI said.
But other traders said the move higher was not justified by indifferent fundamentals and expected prices to start easing back.
Zinc similarly was sticking close to $1,350 closing level and was last indicated at $1,350/53. Traders saw it in a $1,325-$1,360 range near term.
Nickel, which tumbled sharply on Wednesday on commission house and trade selling, was marginally firmer at $7,600, up $40.
"Technically the chart gap (at $7,620-$7,660) has now been filled and...good support should be forthcoming from the 30-day moving average at $7,514," brokers Brandeis said.
Alloy was little changed straddling the $1,500 level.
